items.t: Leprosy (all forms, as part of multi-drug therapy); dermatitis herpetiformis and other dermatoses; malaria prophylaxis with pyrimethamine; Pneumocystis (carinii) pneumonia prophylaxis in immunodeficient patients.

src.q: As part of a multi-drug regimen in the treatment of all forms of leprosy. Treatment of dermatitis herpetiformis and other dermatoses. Prophylaxis of malaria in combination with pyrimethamine.
Prophylaxis of Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia in immunodeficient subjects, especially AIDS patients.

restrictions.note: No specialist-only, shared-care or brand restrictions found in the dapsone SmPCs; no MHRA Drug Safety Update for dapsone found by keyword search; no SPS dapsone monitoring page found.

items.t: Multibacillary leprosy (3-drug regimen), adults and children over 12: 100 mg DAILY for at least 2 years.

src.q: Multibacillary leprosy (3-drug regimen): 100mg daily for at least two years.

items.t: Paucibacillary leprosy (2-drug regimen), adults and children over 12: 100 mg DAILY for at least 6 months.

src.q: Adults and children over 12 years of age:
Paucibacillary leprosy (2-drug regimen): 100mg daily for at least six months.

items.t: Dermatitis herpetiformis, adults and children over 12: start 50 mg DAILY, increase gradually to 300 mg daily if needed; once lesions subside reduce to the minimum (usually 25-50 mg daily), which may continue for years. Gluten-free diet often allows lower maintenance.

src.q: Adults and children over 12 years of age:
Dermatitis herpetiformis: Initially 50mg daily, gradually increasing to 300mg daily if required.
usually 25-50mg daily, which may be continued for a number of years

items.t: Malaria prophylaxis, adults and children over 12: 100 mg ONCE WEEKLY with pyrimethamine 12.5 mg.

src.q: Adults and children over 12 years of age:
Malaria prophylaxis: 100mg weekly with 12.5mg pyrimethamine.

items.t: Pneumocystis pneumonia (with trimethoprim), adults and children over 12: 50-100 mg DAILY, or 100 mg TWICE WEEKLY, or 200 mg ONCE WEEKLY.

src.q: Adults and children over 12 years of age:
Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia: In combination with trimethoprim, 50-100mg daily; 100mg twice weekly or 200mg once weekly.

items.t: Elderly: reduce dose where hepatic function is impaired.

src.q: Dosage should be reduced in the elderly where there is an impairment of hepatic function.

items.t: Children 6-12 years: multibacillary leprosy 50 mg daily for at least 2 years; paucibacillary leprosy 50 mg daily for at least 6 months.

src.q: Children aged 6 years to 12 years: Multibacillary leprosy (3-drug regimen): 50mg daily for at least two years. Paucibacillary leprosy (2-drug regimen): 50mg daily for at least six months.

items.t: Under 6 years: safety and efficacy not established; no data.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of Dapsone in children aged less than six years has not been established. No data are available.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to dapsone, sulfonamides, sulfones or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to dapsone, sulfonamides, sulfones, or any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Severe anaemia; porphyria; severe G6PD deficiency.

src.q: Severe anaemia. Porphyria. Severe glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency.

items.t: Cardiac or pulmonary disease: use with caution.

src.q: Dapsone should be used with caution in patients with cardiac or pulmonary disease.

items.t: Haemolysis: G6PD deficiency, methaemoglobin reductase deficiency or haemoglobin M make patients more susceptible. Subjects with G6PD deficiency are affected by doses above 50 mg daily.

src.q: Patients deficient in glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase, or methaemoglobin reductase, or with haemoglobin M are more susceptible to the haemolytic effects of dapsone.
subjects deficient in glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase are affected by doses above 50mg daily

items.t: Anaemia: use with caution; treat severe anaemia before starting.

src.q: Dapsone should be used with caution in anaemia. Severe anaemia should be treated prior to initiation of dapsone therapy.

items.t: Sulfonamide antibiotic allergy (SPS): dapsone is a sulfone with an arylamine group; up to 20% of sulfonamide-sensitive people also react. After a serious sulfonamide reaction, avoid dapsone if possible.

src.q: Up to 20% of people sensitive to sulfonamide antibiotics also react to dapsone, but most tolerate it without issues.
Even so, people who have had a serious reaction to a sulfonamide antibiotic should avoid dapsone if possible.

items.t: Trimethoprim: increased dapsone and trimethoprim concentrations reported (AIDS patients).

src.q: Increased dapsone and trimethoprim concentrations have been reported following concurrent administration in AIDS patients.

items.t: Probenecid raises dapsone levels; rifampicin increases dapsone clearance (not in master list).

src.q: Excretion of dapsone is reduced and plasma concentrations are increased by concurrent administration of probenecid.
Rifampicin has been reported to increase the plasma clearance of dapsone.

renal.note: No renal dose adjustment or threshold in the dapsone SmPCs. No SPS renal page found.

items.t: Elderly with impaired hepatic function: reduce dose. Hepatitis, jaundice and liver test changes are uncommon adverse effects.

src.q: Dosage should be reduced in the elderly where there is an impairment of hepatic function.
Hepatic disorders Uncommon Hepatitis Jaundice Changes in liver function tests

items.t: SmPC: in leprosy, benefits are generally considered to outweigh any potential risk. Some leprologists recommend folic acid 5 mg daily in pregnancy. No BUMPS leaflet found.

src.q: It is now generally considered that the benefits of dapsone in the treatment of leprosy outweigh any potential risk to the pregnant patient.
Some leprologists recommend 5mg folic acid supplementation daily for leprosy patients receiving dapsone during pregnancy.

items.t: Passes into breast milk; haemolytic anaemia reported in a breastfed infant. Some advise against use in lactation, but leprosy therapy is generally continued.

src.q: Dapsone diffuses into breast milk and there has been a report of haemolytic anaemia in a breast fed infant.
While some feel that dapsone should not be used in lactating mothers, in general therapy for leprosy is continued in such patients.

reproductive.note: No fertility or contraception statements in the dapsone SmPCs; no BUMPS dapsone leaflet found (404).

items.t: Common: haemolysis and methaemoglobinaemia (dose-related; most subjects above 200 mg daily; up to 100 mg daily does not cause significant haemolysis).

src.q: Blood disorders Common Haemolysis1 Methemoglobinaemia1
occurring in most subjects administered more than 200mg daily
doses of up to 100mg daily do not cause significant haemolysis

items.t: Agranulocytosis (rare; more often with other malaria prophylaxis medicines).

src.q: this is rare when dapsone is used alone, reports are more common when dapsone has been used with other medicines for malarial prophylaxis

items.t: Dapsone syndrome (after 3-6 weeks: rash, fever, eosinophilia): stop immediately; can progress to exfoliative dermatitis, hepatitis, psychosis; deaths recorded.

src.q: this may occur following 3-6 weeks of therapy, symptoms include rash, (always present), fever, and eosinophilia.
If dapsone is not stopped immediately; the syndrome may progress to exfoliative dermatitis, hepatitis, albuminuria and psychosis. Deaths have been recorded.

items.t: Severe skin reactions (rare): exfoliative dermatitis, TEN, SJS.

src.q: Rare Maculopapular rash Exfoliative dermatitis Toxic epidermal necrolysis Stevens-Johnson syndrome

items.t: Severe lepra reactions affecting eyes or nerves: stop or reduce dapsone.

src.q: Dapsone should be discontinued or reduced in dosage if severe lepra reactions affecting the eyes or nerve trunks occur.

items.t: Treat severe anaemia before starting.

src.q: Severe anaemia should be treated prior to initiation of dapsone therapy.

items.t: Regular blood counts during treatment (no interval stated in the SmPC).

src.q: It is recommended that regular blood counts be performed during treatment with dapsone.

items.t: Stop immediately if dapsone syndrome (rash with fever and eosinophilia) develops.

src.q: If dapsone is not stopped immediately; the syndrome may progress to exfoliative dermatitis

items.t: Oral. Note the different frequencies by indication: DAILY (leprosy, dermatitis herpetiformis), WEEKLY (malaria prophylaxis), daily or twice/once weekly (Pneumocystis).
